Playbook.name: AD — DCSync: Directory Replication by an Unexpected Principal - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A principal that is not a domain controller requested directory-replication rights (4662 with the DS-Replication-Get-Changes GUIDs). Triage question: was the requesting account actually a DC/approved replication identity, or a user/host abusing replication to pull password hashes?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: DCSync extracts any account's NTLM hash - including krbtgt - straight from AD, enabling Golden Tickets and full domain compromise.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: Replication access
Signal.Details: 4662 AccessMask 0x100 with the replication property GUIDs 1131f6aa/1131f6ad/9923a32a; SYSTEM excluded.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the 4662 was logged (a DC).

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Source IP if present in the alert.

InitialAssessment.Rule: If $username resolves to a domain controller computer account or the documented AAD-Connect/Azure sync account, likely benign - VERIFY against the approved list.
Any interactive user or non-DC host requesting replication is treated as TP until proven otherwise.

Investigation.Goal: Confirm whether $username is an approved replication identity; if not, scope what it accessed and where the session originated.

Step.name: Confirm the requesting principal and repetition
Step.Purpose: Approved replication comes from DC computer accounts (name$) or the AAD sync account; anything else is the finding.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4662" AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS accesses = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), dcs = VALUES(host.name), masks = VALUES(winlog.event_data.AccessMask) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A DC computer account ends in $ and appears constantly (normal replication). An interactive human/service name here = DCSync abuse. Note whether it hit multiple DCs.

Step.name: Where is this principal logged on from (foothold)
Step.Purpose: A non-DC principal doing DCSync is running from a foothold - find the source host/session.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$username" AND event.code == "4624" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Identify the workstation/server the principal is operating from; that host is the pivot for containment. Network logon (type 3) into a DC from a workstation just before the 4662 is the classic DCSync-from-foothold trail.

Step.name: Did the same principal grant itself the rights recently (4670/5136)
Step.Purpose: Attackers often add replication rights just before using them; a matching permission change is strong intent evidence.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4670","5136") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND (winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" OR winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$username") | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.ObjectName, winlog.event_data.AttributeLDAPDisplayName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A recent DACL/permission change adding Get-Changes rights to this principal, followed by the replication, is near-conclusive TP.

Node.Condition: INV-01 principal is NOT a DC computer account or the approved sync identity (an interactive/service account or non-DC host).
Node.Result: True Positive (DCSync - domain compromise, immediate IR)

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows the principal recently granted itself replication rights before using them.
Node.Result: True Positive (DCSync with privilege setup - immediate IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 principal is a known DC computer account ($) or the documented Azure AD Connect/MSOL sync account replicating normally.
Principal identity/role cannot be confirmed against the approved replication list.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-DCSYNC-WHO, INV-02-DCSYNC-SESSION, INV-03-DCSYNC-GRANT to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Legitimate directory replication by a DC or the approved directory-sync identity.

Indicators.Item: SubjectUserName is a DC computer account (ends in $) or the documented MSOL_/AAD sync account.
Behavior is continuous and historical, not first-seen.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the principal against the approved replication allowlist.
Close as false_positive; add to the allowlist if missing.

TruePositive.Definition: Abuse of replication rights to extract password hashes from AD.

Indicators.Item: Session originates from a workstation/server foothold.

SOCAction.Item: Treat as domain compromise: isolate the foothold host, disable the principal.
Rotate krbtgt TWICE and reset privileged/service accounts.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A monitoring/backup tool mis-granted replication rights it does not truly need.

Indicators.Item: A known backup/monitoring service account with replication rights it was over-provisioned.
Vendor confirms the tool reads directory data legitimately but should not have Get-Changes.

SOCAction.Item: Remove excess replication rights; validate the tool still functions.
Document; do not treat as incident if provenance is clean.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Isolate the foothold host from INV-02.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Rotate krbtgt twice; reset all privileged and service accounts; revoke tickets.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Tighten replication ACLs to DCs + approved sync account only.
Alert on replication-rights DACL changes (INV-03 pattern) as its own detection.

QualityChecks.Check: Replication GUIDs and AccessMask 0x100 verified in the rule; SYSTEM excluded.
Maintain the approved-replication allowlist for fast triage.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Principal confirmed on the approved replication allowlist.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: krbtgt rotated x2, privileged accounts reset, foothold eradicated, tickets revoked.
